an10.17:1.6: In that respect, a mendicant is ethical … they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.
an10.17:2.2: In that respect, a mendicant is very learned … penetrating them theoretically.
an10.17:3.2: In that respect, a mendicant has good friends, companions, and associates.
an10.17:4.2: In that respect, a mendicant is easy to admonish … take instruction respectfully.
an10.17:5.2: In that respect, a mendicant in the duties of their spiritual companions … able to complete and organize the work.
an10.17:6.2: In that respect, a mendicant loves the teachings and is a delight to converse with, being full of joy in the teaching and training.
an10.17:7.2: In that respect, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.
an10.17:8.2: In that respect, a mendicant is content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
an10.17:9.2: In that respect, a mendicant is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.
an10.17:10.2: In that respect, a mendicant is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
